cards.explanation: The answer is donkey, friends. Jesus says they'll find one tied there, with her colt beside her (Matthew 21:2). He tells them to untie both and bring them to Him. Two animals, one errand, and the disciples get the whole plan before they even leave.

The answer is True, friends! Jesus says, “If anyone questions you, tell him that the Lord needs them, and he will send them right away.” (Matthew 21:3) So the answer to the question is already in the disciples' pockets. Jesus hands them the whole script before they even leave.

The answer is her King, friends! The prophet says, “See, your King comes to you…” (Matthew 21:5) The Daughter of Zion is Jerusalem's people, and the King is coming to HER. Not sending a letter, not calling ahead. Coming.

The answer is gentle, friends! The prophet says the King comes “…gentle and riding on a donkey, on a colt, the foal of a donkey.” (Matthew 21:5) Kings usually show up with a big loud entrance, so I think a gentle King on a donkey is a surprise. That's the word the text picks for Him.

The answer is False, friends! The disciples “…laid their cloaks on them, and Jesus sat on them.” (Matthew 21:7) The cloaks go on the animals, and Jesus rides. That's just what the prophet said, a King riding on a donkey (Matthew 21:5).

The answer is cloaks AND branches, friends! “A massive crowd spread their cloaks on the road, while others cut branches from the trees and spread them on the road.” (Matthew 21:8) Some spread cloaks, and others cut branches from the trees. Both of them end up on the road for Jesus.
The answer is the Son of David, friends! The crowds shout, “Hosanna to the Son of David!” (Matthew 21:9) Those in front of Him and those behind Him are shouting. That's the first line the text gives.
The answer is False, friends! When Jesus enters, the whole city is stirred and asks, “Who is this?” (Matthew 21:10) That's a city asking about Him. The crowds reply in the next verse (Matthew 21:11).

The answer is the prophet from Nazareth in Galilee, friends! The crowds reply, “This is Jesus, the prophet from Nazareth in Galilee.” (Matthew 21:11) That's the answer they give the stirred city. A name, a title and a hometown, all in one breath.
